## Goal

Audit generated functions that appear reusable and pass convenient examples
but do not preserve boundary, missing-value, or argument behavior.

## Scenario

Download:

- [week11-ai-refactor-review.R](../code/r/week11-ai-refactor-review.R)
- [week10-service-events.csv](../data/week10-service-events.csv)

Keep the CSV inside a `data` folder, then run the review script.

## Part A: Threshold Function

The intended rule counts a response at exactly the target as within target and
maps missing response time to `FALSE`. The generated function uses `<` and
returns `NA` for missing input.

Complete:

| Input | Intended | Generated | Contract exposed |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `4.5` |  |  | ordinary case |
| `12` |  |  | exact boundary |
| `13` |  |  | above boundary |
| `NA` |  |  | missing-value policy |

## Part B: Unused Argument

The generated summary accepts `issue_name` but always filters to `"hvac"`.

Compare intended and generated results for `"hvac"`, `"access"`, and
`"lighting"`. Explain why testing only HVAC gives false confidence.

## Part C: Repair Both Functions

Restore the inclusive threshold and explicit missing-value behavior. Replace
the hard-coded issue with the argument and validate that the requested category
exists.

## Part D: Behavior-Preservation Table

Complete:

|---|---|---|---|
| accepted inputs |  |  |  |
| default target |  |  |  |
| threshold boundary |  |  |  |
| missing-value output |  |  |  |

| invalid-input behavior |  |  |  |

## Part E: Write A Minimal Test Suite

Create the smallest set of tests that catches both generated errors. Explain
why each test is necessary and which redundant tests could be removed.

## Deliverable

Submit the completed tables, repaired functions, minimal test suite, and a
5-7 sentence explanation of why passing examples do not prove that a refactor
preserves behavior.
